claim:
Let \(G=K_{a,b,c}\) be a finite complete tripartite graph with \(a\ge b\ge c\ge1\) and \(N=a+b+c\). For the global coalition number \(GC(G)\),
\[GC(K_{a,b,c})=\begin{cases}a+1,&c=1,\\N-2,&c=2,\\N-3,&c\ge3.\end{cases}\]
Moreover, a vertex set of \(K_{a,b,c}\) is globally dominating if and only if it meets all three partite sets. Thus global-coalition partners are governed exactly by union of part-supports, and the displayed formula resolves the complete tripartite case beyond the previously available complete-multipartite lower bound \(GC(K_{n_1,\ldots,n_m})\ge n_1+n_m\).
integrity: All mathematical assertions in the finding are proved self-containedly. The source supplies the invariant definition and prior complete-multipartite lower-bound context, not the new exact formula. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to complete tripartite graphs; the packaged finite verifier covers orders at most \(10\) only and is corroborative. The current arXiv record is withdrawn because of issues in a later revision, so the argument relies only on version-1 definitions/context and independently rederives all mathematical premises used. A differently indexed equivalent result may still exist.
title: Global coalition numbers of complete tripartite graphs
